args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED AT THE REQUEST OF COUNSEL

MEMORANDUM

TO:      Deal Team — Funds Asset Management
FROM:    [Associate], Funds & Asset Management Practice
RE:      Redline Review of Counterparty Markup of Investment Advisory Agreement
MATTER:  Matter File 15 — Funds Asset Management
DATE:    August 10, 2026

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
I.   INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have been asked to review the counterparty's redlined markup of the
Investment Advisory Agreement against (i) our firm's standard form, (ii) the
internal negotiation playbook, (iii) the operative deal materials (including
the disclosure schedules and exhibits), and (iv) the applicable regulatory
framework governing registered investment advisers under the Investment
Advisers Act of 1940, as amended (the "Advisers Act"), the rules and
regulations thereunder, and relevant SEC interpretive guidance. This
memorandum identifies each material deviation introduced by the counterparty,
reconciles those deviations against the base materials, and sets out
recommended positions informed by the controlling partner instructions on
this engagement.

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions. Its markup
introduces a focused set of deviations that, in combination, would
substantially reallocate risk and cost from the adviser-client relationship.
The material deviations are:

   (1)  a silent reduction of the indemnification cap;
   (2)  conversion of the indemnification basket from a true deductible to a
        tipping basket;
   (3)  the addition of carve-outs to the definition of "Material Adverse
        Effect" ("MAE") addressing regulatory action of exactly the kind at
        issue in this matter; and
   (4)  a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core
        representations.

Each deviation is analyzed below against the standard form, the playbook, the
disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the regulatory framework. Consistent
with the controlled engagement instructions and the scheduled exceptions
governing the transaction, the client has authorized concession of the basket
conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
II.  CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS AND PRIORITIES
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The deal-team correspondence controls the analysis priorities for this
engagement. The latest partner communication REVISES the earlier priority
ordering and is controlling over any superseded instruction in the thread:

   o  The client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion (the conversion of the
      indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket).
   o  The client TREATS ANY SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION AS A WALK-AWAY ISSUE.
      A counterparty reduction of the survival period for the core
      representations is not negotiable and, if insisted upon, would
      constitute a deal-breaker requiring the transaction to be terminated.

The deliverable reflects this controlling instruction. Any analysis that
appears inconsistent with the earlier (superseded) priority ordering should
be disregarded.

In addition, under the operative scheduling convention, the scheduled
exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. Any
analysis must reconcile the counterparty markup against BOTH the firm-standard
base materials AND the disclosure schedules and exhibits, giving the
scheduled exceptions priority.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION 1 — REDUCTION OF THE INDEMNIFICATION CAP
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Counterparty Markup

The counterparty's markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. The
standard form measures the indemnification cap at the fees paid or payable
over the twenty-four (24) months preceding the claim (the standard measurement
period for services/indemnity obligations in our funds practice). The markup
would shrink the cap and thereby materially reduce the adviser's exposure for
indemnifiable claims.

B.  Standard Form / Playbook Position

Our funds asset management standard form measures the indemnification cap at
the fees paid or payable in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the claim.
The internal playbook treats this as the standard position. The playbook
identifies an approved fallback floor of eighteen (18) months; any reduction
to a twelve (12) month measurement period is below the approved fallback floor
and requires escalation to the appropriate approver. This is consistent with
the firm-wide drafting guidance that cap reductions must be quantified at the
current monthly run-rate under the agreement in negotiation.

B.  Analysis

The silent reduction of the indemnification cap is a material economic
concession that cannot be accepted without quantification and escalation. We
have quantified the impact of the reduction against the current monthly
run-rate of the agreement in negotiation. The reduction would lower the cap
from the standard twenty-four (24) month fee-based measurement to a
materially lower figure, exposing a gap that would leave the client (as
adviser) bearing un-indemnified exposure for claims that should sit with the
counterparty.

Under the playbook, if the counterparty's proposed measurement period falls
below the approved fallback floor of eighteen (18) months, approval from the
stated approver is required before any concession may be offered or accepted.
The reduction is also unauthorized relative to the deal team's delegated
authority and must be escalated before any position is taken.

D.  Recommended Position

   o  REJECT the reduction of the indemnification cap as marked.
   o  Hold to the standard twenty-four (24) month fee-based cap.
   o  If concession is required to close, the maximum authorized fallback is
      the eighteen (18) month measurement period; any further reduction
      requires escalation to the stated approver with a quantified escalation
      memorandum showing the cap value at the standard measurement period,
      at the counterparty's proposed period, and at the approved fallback
      floor.
   o  This deviation does NOT intersect the client's authorized concession
      (which is limited to the basket conversion) and so must be defended.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV.  DEVIATION 2 — CONVERSION OF THE BASKET FROM A DEDUCTIBLE TO A
     TIPPING BASKET
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Counterparty Markup

The counterparty's markup converts the indemnification basket from a true
deductible to a tipping basket. Under a deductible, the indemnifying party
bears losses only above the basket threshold; under a tipping basket, once
the threshold is reached the indemnifying party becomes liable for the entire
amount from the first dollar.

B.  Standard Form / Playbook Position

Our standard form and internal playbook require that the basket remain a true
deductible. In our funds practice, conversion to a tipping basket is out of
policy at any threshold because it materially increases the adviser's
aggregate exposure once the basket is crossed.

C.  Analysis and Authorized Concession

Notwithstanding the standard-fall policy position against a tipping basket,
the controlling partner instruction on this engagement expressly directs that
the client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion. The client has made a
commercial decision to accept the tipping-basket mechanic in order to move
the transaction forward. Consistent with the controlled instruction, we
recommend ACCEPTING the basket conversion as a commercial concession.

The concession should be documented, and the dollar threshold at which the
tipping mechanism activates should be confirmed to be at or above the
standard deductible/basket floor. The concession is limited to the mechanism
itself and does not extend to any reduction of the cap (Deviation 1) or to the
survival-period reduction (Deviation 4), both of which remain separately
subject to analysis below.

D.  Recommended Position

   o  ACCEPT the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket), consistent
      with the controlling client instruction.
   o  Confirm the activation threshold remains at or above the standard
      basket floor.
   o  Document the concession for the record and ensure it is not used as a
      predicate to undermine the cap or survival positions.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
V.   DEVIATION 3 — MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Counterparty Markup

The counterparty's markup adds carve-outs to the definition of "Material
Adverse Effect" that address regulatory action. Critically, the carve-outs are
drafted to encompass regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this
matter — namely, the regulatory inquiries that are the subject of Schedule 3.7.

B.  Interaction with Schedule 3.7

Schedule 3.7 discloses two (2) pending regulatory inquiries. The counterparty's
proposed MAE carve-outs are calibrated to the precise subject matter of those
inquiries. If accepted as marked, the MAE definition would exclude from
"Material Adverse Effect" the very regulatory developments that arise from the
disclosed inquiries, thereby stripping the client of the ability to treat
adverse regulatory outcomes as an MAE. This is a device to immunize the
counterparty against the consequences of the disclosed pendency while
otherwise narrowing the circumstances in which an MAE may be found.

Per the control instruction that scheduled exceptions control over general
statements, the present analysis must honor the Schedule 3.7 disclosures.
The markup's carve-outs operate to unwind what Schedule 3.7 otherwise
places on the record.

C.  Regulatory Framework

Registered investment advisers owe their clients fiduciary duties under
Section 206 of the Advisers Act (prohibiting fraudulent, deceptive, or
manipulative practices and requiring full disclosure of conflicts of
interest). An MAE definition that excludes regulatory action arising from
disclosed ongoing inquiries — combined with the adviser's ongoing disclosure
obligations and duty of care — could create a gap where the client/adviser is
obligated to continue performing notwithstanding a regulatory development
that materially undermines the investment program. The carve-out must be
analyzed for consistency with the adviser's regulatory obligations and the
client's ability to respond.

D.  Recommended Position

   o  REJECT the MAE carve-outs as drafted, which are narrowly tailored to
      the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.
   o  If counterparty presses for regulatory carve-outs, limit any such
      carve-out to regulatory developments that are (i) immaterial in the
      aggregate, or (ii) the direct result of the disclosed Schedule 3.7
      matters only to the extent they do not constitute an MAE under the
      otherwise-applicable standard.
   o  Preserve the client's ability to invoke an MAE based on regulatory
      action arising from the disclosed inquiries.
   o  Flag for escalation; do not concede without client sign-off.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
VI.  DEVIATION 4 — LIMITATION PERIOD SHORTENING SURVIVAL OF CORE
     REPRESENTATIONS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Counterparty Markup

The counterparty's markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the
survival period for the core representations. This directly contradicts the
survival matrix set out in Exhibit B.

B.  Interaction with Exhibit B

Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the representations. The markup's
limitation-period change would reduce the survival period below the Exhibit B
matrix. Under the scheduling control instruction, the Exhibit B survival
matrix is the operative baseline; the counterparty's proposed limitation
period contradicts it.

C.  Analysis and Authorized Position

This is the second of the two controlling-priority items. The partner
instruction treats ANY SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION AS A WALK-AWAY ISSUE. A
survival-period reduction is therefore a non-negotiable, deal-breaker item.
The counterparty must withdraw the reduced limitation period and conform the
survival provisions to the Exhibit B matrix. If the counterparty persists in
seeking any shortening of the survival period, the firm should treat the
matter as at impasse and proceed to walk away from the transaction rather
than accept the reduction.

This is consistent with the regulatory context: preserving a sufficient
survival period for the core representations is essential to maintaining
meaningful recourse and to the orderly close of the investment relationship.
A shortened survival period would materially undermine the client's ability
to pursue claims for breaches of the fundamental representations.

D.  Recommended Position

   o  REJECT, AND DO NOT CONCEDE, any survival-period reduction.
   o  Require the counterparty to conform the limitation period to the
        Exhibit B survival matrix.
   o  TREAT THE SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION AS A WALK-AWAY ISSUE. If the
        counterparty will not withdraw the reduction, recommend termination
        of the transaction in accordance with the client's controlling
        instruction.
   o  Quantify the exposure created by the shortened survival period at the
        current run-rate so the deal team can assess the walk-away decision
        with full information.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. DEVIATION 5 — INTERACTION OF INDEMNIFICATION CHANGES WITH SCHEDULE
     5.2 RETAINED LIABILITIES
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.  Schedule 5.2

Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that would be silently shifted by the
counterparty's indemnification changes. Because the counterparty reduces the
indemnification cap (Deviation 1), converts the basket to a tipping basket
(Deviation 2), and narrows the MAE definition (Deviation 3), the aggregate
effect is to shift a larger share of the disclosed retained liabilities from
the counterparty back to the client/adviser.

B.  Analysis

The cumulative operation of the markup's indemnification changes would
reallocate the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities in a manner inconsistent
with the commercial allocation reflected in the base materials. Even where
each individual change might appear minor, the combined effect on Schedule
5.2 is material because the Schedule 5.2 liabilities sit precisely in the
areas carved out by the MAE modifications and the reduced cap.

Per the control principle that scheduled exceptions control over general
statements, the Schedule 5.2 disclosures fix the retained-liability baseline.
The markup's changes must not operate to shift those liabilities silently. The
markup cannot be accepted insofar as it erodes the Schedule 5.2 allocation
without an explicit, identified commercial trade.

C.  Recommended Position

   o  REJECT any operation of the markup that would shift the Schedule 5.2
      retained liabilities to the client.
   o  Confirm that the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain allocated to
      the counterparty in accordance with the base materials, notwithstanding
      the basket conversion (which the client has conceded) and the cap
      position.
   o  Reconcile the cumulative effect of Deviations 1, 2, and 3 against
      Schedule 5.2 before the markup is accepted in any form.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
VIII. REGULATORY FRAMEWORK OVERVIEW (FUNDS ASSET MANAGEMENT)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Investment Advisory Agreement is governed by, and must operate consistently
with, the Advisers Act and the rules thereunder. Key considerations relevant to
this review include:

   o  Fiduciary duties. Registered investment advisers are fiduciaries to their
      clients. They must act in the client's best interest and disclose all
      material conflicts of interest. Indemnification and liability-allocation
      provisions that erode the client's protection must be scrutinized for
      consistency with these duties.
   o  Delegation and authority. Under Section 205 of the Advisers Act, advisory
      contracts may not permit assignment without client consent, and certain
      performance-fee arrangements are restricted. Any markup touching
      delegation or fee structure must be reviewed for compliance.
   o  Disclosure and materiality. MAE carve-outs that are calibrated to
      disclosed regulatory inquiries create tension with the adviser's ongoing
      disclosure obligations and with the accuracy of prior disclosures.
   o  Form ADV and regulatory filings. The counterparty's markup of survival and
      MAE provisions is not a securities-law compliance item per se, but the 
      negotiation must not create contractual provisions that would conflict
      with the adviser's regulatory filing obligations.

The deviation analysis above is grounded in this framework, particularly the
fiduciary-duty overlay that argues against accepting indemnification,
MAE, and survival changes that shift risk to the adviser in a manner
inconsistent with the client's disclosed regulatory posture.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IX.  SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDED POSITIONS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   DEVIATION                             RECOMMENDED POSITION
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. Indemnification cap reduction      REJECT; hold to standard
                                         (24-month fee-based) cap; maximum
                                         fallback 18 months; escalate if
                                         below floor.

   2. Basket conversion (deductible →    ACCEPT (authorized concession) per
      tipping basket)                    controlling client instruction;
                                         confirm threshold at/below
                                         standard floor.

   3. MAE carve-outs for regulatory      REJECT as drafted (tailored to
      action                             Schedule 3.7 inquiries); preserve
                                         client MAE rights; escalate before
                                         any concession.

   4. Survival-period reduction          REJECT; WALK-AWAY ISSUE; conform
      (limitation period)                to Exhibit B survival matrix;
                                         recommend termination if not
                                         withdrawn.

   5. Schedule 5.2 retained-liability    REJECT silent shift; confirm
      shift (cumulative cap/basket/MAE   liabilities remain with
      effect)                            counterparty.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
X.   ESCALATIONS AND OPEN ITEMS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   o  Escalate Deviation 1 (indemnification cap reduction) if the counterparty
      will not return to the standard or approved-fallback measurement period,
      with a quantified escalation memorandum showing the cap value at the
      standard measurement period, at the counterparty's proposed period, and
      at the approved fallback floor.
   o  Escalate Deviation 3 (MAE carve-outs) before any concession; obtain
      client sign-off on the treatment of the Schedule 3.7 regulatory
      inquiries.
   o  Deviation 4 is a walk-away item. If the counterparty will not withdraw
      the survival-period reduction, recommend terminating the transaction in
      accordance with the controlling client instruction. No further
      negotiation should be undertaken on this point absent client reversal.
   o  Confirm the basket-conversion threshold (Deviation 2, conceded) is not
      used as leverage to obtain the cap or survival concessions.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------
XI.  CONCLUSION
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

The counterparty's markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces
four material deviations that would significantly reallocate risk and cost.
In accordance with the controlling client instructions, the client concedes
the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away
issue. The indemnification cap reduction, the MAE carve-outs, and the Schedule
5.2 retained-liability shift must be defended and, where noted, escalated. The
cumulative effect of the markup, reconciled against Schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and
Exhibit B, would otherwise erode the protections central to the investment
advisory relationship and conflict with the regulatory framework governing
registered investment advisers.

We are available to finalize markups incorporating the recommended positions
and to prepare any escalation memoranda required by the playbook.
